headline: Move in: HOMEBODY, a whole little life
lede: The arcade got people. Two residents, five needs, one suburban lot and a clock that never stops — an original life sim in the spirit of the 2000 classic, built entirely in code and playable by tap.

notes.text: #899 shipped as HOMEBODY: tap a fridge, bed, TV or mailbox and your resident walks over and does the thing — needs drain, moods glow, and Fern the neighbour rings the bell.

Buy mode freezes time over thirteen furniture pieces; a connectivity guard refuses any placement that would wall a resident in — it earned that rule the hard way when a bed sealed a bedroom and the whole demo starved.
Autonomy is now a demo-only mode: the attract sim lives its own life, but in your hands the residents wait for orders — ignore them and the household really does fall apart.
Three gates on the way in: peoplecheck 35/35 with a mutation that correctly went red, contractcheck 14/14, and a real-Chrome drive 17/17 from move-in to eviction and back.
